children: Shares of Clover Health Investments rose after the company said its 2027 PPO Medicare Advantage plans were rated five stars by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services.
The stock gained 11%, to $5.09, after hours Thursday. It closed up 0.4%, at $4.58, and has nearly doubled in value this year.
The company also said its HMO Medicare Advantage plan was assigned a 4.5-star rating.

Clover won a legal challenge earlier this year over CMS's previous rating for the company's PPO plans, which the agency recalculated to 4.5 stars from 3.5 stars following a ruling in a Georgia federal court. The case is currently on appeal, Clover said.
CMS removed 20 measures from its recent calculations in accordance with the ruling, the company said Thursday, adding that the PPO plans would have scored 4.5 stars had the measures been included.

Clover Health Chief Executive Andrew Toy said the company remains in favor of "reforms to the Stars program that more closely align these ratings with meaningful improvements in members' health and value for the Medicare program."
Clover's Medicare Advantage membership grew 48% year-over-year through the first half of 2026, the company said. Of those members, 98% are enrolled in wide-network PPO plans.
